title: One method, one node — the single-frame gate

frames.title: SubInvoker.Apply
frames.explanation: The commonest case there is: one method, one file, no call chain. Round 3 judged this against the in-place spotlight it replaced and it won, which is why there is only one surface now.

relations.note: the accumulator, from its first assignment to its last read

steps.ttsText: Apply takes the already-scaled amount and the shared options, refuses a null options object, and asks it to validate itself before anything is computed.

steps.note: Registration order, not priority order — the registry is what decides.
steps.ttsText: Then each enabled adjustment runs over the running total in registration order, and every one of them is recorded with the value it started from.
Finally it guards against a negative total and returns it rounded to the configured precision, leaving the amount untouched when it is already rounded.
